messages:
maria: Heads up — we plan to remove the client-priv-route-shim from the internal proxy on 2026-05-15. It injects a hidden affinity header and is causing quota duplication and telemetry blindspots. Need SDK teams + console UX aware so customers don't get surprised.
sam: Quick ask — is the root cause just quota duplication or are there other safety concerns?
maria: Primarily quota duplication. The shim sets `X-Client-Priv-Route` to force affinity for old clients; that header bypasses the quota normalizer and also isn't sampled correctly in our ingestion pipeline (so we lose route metadata). It's inflating per-route counts and screwing per-customer cost estimates.
raj: SDK impact: Python/TS/Go clients currently default to preserving the shim to avoid regressions. If we flip/remove it without a migration flag that'll be a breaking change.
tessa: Proposal: deprecate with a staged plan — emit warnings, add telemetry to identify senders, provide SDK opt-out flag, surface a console migration tile, canary the removal behind a legacy pool for 2w, then flip default after 30–45d. No immediate hard-break.
sam: Console/telemetry ask: add a tile in the Rollouts dashboard showing "Shim users" (count by customer + sample requests). Also show an estimated cost delta if they drop the shim (we can compute from quota-normalized counts).
maria: Agreed. Also want a lightweight telemetry event when the header is present: `shim_deprecate_v1` with customer_id, route, and sampling=1/100. @ops-bot can you start emitting that?
ops-bot: ack — telemetry event `shim_deprecate_v1` emitted starting 3799000005; sampled at 1/100 by default, includes customer_id and route when available.
raj: Working on SDK patches. Python snippet for an opt-out API:
```python
# opt-out of injecting the legacy shim
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(preserve_route_shim=False)
```
I'll ship as a minor version and add a runtime `warnings.warn` whenever the header is present. TS/Go will have equivalent flags.
sam: Nice. For the Rollouts UX: add a quick migration CTA that links to the SDK doc. We should also show the percent of traffic still using the shim and a suggested canary policy (e.g., 5% -> 25% -> 100%).
tessa: Canary + quota reconciliation job: after canary starts, run a 7-day diff job that surfaces token/cost deltas in the console and flags regressed evals if any.
maria: Owners/TLDR: eng-platform (sam) handles proxy flips and legacy pool; SDKs (raj) deliver opt-out + warning; devex (maria/tessa) draft migration guide + console tile. Timeline: announce today, enable telemetry flags in 48h, experimental SDK opt-out in 7d, console tile in 10d, start canary in ~21d, flip default in 45d.
sam: I'll open the platform PR and add the deploy plan (legacy pool, rate limits, canary tag). Who's writing customer comms?
maria: I'll draft the comms and migration doc. Raj + Tessa please review.
raj: Quick Q — do we keep fallback routing in proxy for non-updated clients? I vote yes for 90 days; move them to legacy pool and throttle if necessary.
tessa: +1. fallback + rate-limited legacy pool for 90d, then remove.
maria: :rocket: thanks all. I'll post a follow-up RFC doc in #rfc and tag owners. If anyone wants to be on the canary list DM me.
sam: :thumbsup: logging action items on the platform board now.
